_doc.purpose: Machine-readable manifest of the 2026-08-26 problem-taxonomy consolidation. Records every retired problem slug with its destination, class, and rationale; phrase moves between surviving problems; unregistered-phrase attachments; new problems; and relabels. scripts/prerender.mjs reads merges[] to emit a redirect page at /problem/<retired>/ for every retired slug, and scripts/check.mjs validates the manifest against the live registry (no retired slug may be live, every destination must be live, redirects must exist in dist). Append-only: future merges add entries here.
_doc.classes: A exact alias · B surface duplicate (same contract, different wording) · C parent-child inflation (narrow presentation of the same contract) · D method-as-problem (solution family stood as a problem) · E domain specialization that does not change the contract

merges.reason: DPLL (retired-side ancestor lineage sits in boolean-satisfiability) and CDCL solve the identical contract: decide satisfiability of a propositional CNF formula. "SAT solving" was the activity name for the same problem. The one non-SAT phrase, SMT solving (DPLL(T)), moves to the SMT problem instead: satisfiability modulo theories has a materially different input contract and stays distinct per the SAT-vs-SMT non-merge rule.

The split was already incoherent: AC-3 (Maintaining arc consistency) lived inside constraint-satisfaction while AC-4 and AC-2001, the same arc-consistency family, lived outside it. Propagation levels (forward checking, MAC, bounds consistency, alldifferent filtering) are the inference dial inside the one contract: find an assignment satisfying all constraints. Forward checking vs MAC vs backjumping is the classic rival set of CSP solving.

The oracle boundary this label implied was never respected by the data: gradient descent, Newton, and trust-region methods already lived inside continuous-optimization. One contract: minimize a continuous objective over R^n. First-order, quasi-Newton, proximal, and constrained regimes are preserved as phrases; convex structured classes with their own theory (nonsmooth convex, conic, finite-sum, linear/integer programming) remain separate problems.

Every metaheuristic already inside continuous-optimization (evolution strategies, differential evolution, the swarm family) is itself derivative-free, and CMA-ES (here) is literally an evolution strategy (there). Same contract, zeroth-order oracle: minimize a continuous black-box objective. Nelder-Mead vs CMA-ES vs the swarm zoo is one rival set.

K-medoids with PAM swap search (inside clustering) and local-search k-median with swap improvements (here) are the same algorithmic idea filed as two problems. K-center, k-median, and k-means are sibling center-based objectives of one partition-into-k-groups contract; the phrases keep each objective distinct. Facility location is genuinely different (opening costs, cluster count not fixed) and becomes its own problem.

Pollaczek-Khinchine (inside queueing-performance, phrase Single-queue analysis) is itself a waiting-time formula; Kingman and Allen-Cunneen are its GI/G/1 approximations and Lindley its exact recursion. One contract: given arrival and service processes, compute performance measures of the queue.

Shallow embeddings (DeepWalk, node2vec, LINE, struc2vec) and graph neural networks produce the same output contract, vector representations of nodes for downstream tasks, and the shallow-vs-GNN comparison is the canonical bake-off of this literature. Survivor keeps the standard umbrella label Graph representation learning.

Message-passing mutual exclusion protocols (Ricart-Agrawala, Maekawa, Suzuki-Kasami) and lease-based locking with fencing tokens answer the same contract: at most one holder of exclusive access across a distributed system. Leases-vs-protocol is the real deployment tradeoff (failure tolerance vs message optimality).

Latent semantic indexing vs the vector space model and BM25 is the textbook rivalry of one contract: given a query, return a ranked list of relevant documents. Query-expansion entries are end-to-end retrieval configurations over the same benchmark. Survivor relabeled Document ranking and retrieval.

Markov chain analysis already spans stationary behavior, hitting times, and simulation; time-t distributions (uniformization, Krylov matrix exponentials) are another output of the same contract: compute quantitative behavior of a given Markov chain. Simulation vs uniformization is a genuine method choice for transient measures.

Matrix-geometric and spectral-expansion methods compute stationary behavior of structured (QBD) chains: the same contract exploiting structure, exactly as Sparse linear systems and Tridiagonal systems are phrases of Solving linear systems rather than separate problems.

Quantize vs prune vs distill is the standard model-compression trilemma: one contract, produce a smaller or faster model at bounded accuracy loss. Low-precision training (mixed precision, FP8) is not model compression at all, it is a training-efficiency technique, and moves to memory-efficient training beside ZeRO and gradient checkpointing.

Spelling correction is the restricted case of the text-correction contract (map erroneous text to corrected text); noisy-channel and SymSpell correctors are genuine rivals of sequence-to-sequence grammar correction for the fix-user-text job. Survivor keeps the umbrella label Text correction and editing.

Grammar-constrained and JSON-schema decoding are token-masking strategies implemented inside the decoding loop, beside beam, nucleus, and speculative decoding: the same contract (produce an output sequence from a language model), with constraints preserved as a phrase. Survivor relabeled Text decoding and constrained generation.

A solution family promoted to a problem: 2-opt, 3-opt, and Or-opt solve the traveling salesman problem, and Lin-Kernighan, the deluxe member of the same move family, was already inside traveling-salesman. The split kept 2-opt and Lin-Kernighan from being rivals.

One contract: string plus context-free grammar to parse tree or rejection. LL/LR/PEG parsers are the restricted-grammar-class specializations and Earley/CYK/GLR the general-grammar methods; choosing between ANTLR-style LL, LALR, GLR, and PEG is one engineering decision, and GLR exists precisely to continue LR beyond determinism. Grammar-class restrictions survive as phrases. Survivor relabeled Context-free parsing.

Needleman-Wunsch is weighted edit distance; Hirschberg computes the LCS alignment that edit-distance already owns as Sequence similarity; banded alignment and Ukkonen bounded edit distance are the same diagonal-restriction idea filed twice. One pairwise-comparison contract with global/local/bounded/linear-space regimes preserved as phrases. Survivor relabeled Edit distance and sequence alignment.

A method family promoted to a problem. The adversarial MCTS variants (UCT, RAVE, PUCT, parallel MCTS, flat Monte Carlo) choose moves in perfect-information games: the same contract as alpha-beta search, and alpha-beta vs MCTS is the central rivalry this site teaches. Nested Monte Carlo and NRPA are single-agent puzzle searches and move to puzzle-state search instead.

A method-family label (learning dynamics) whose members compute equilibria of two different game classes. The CFR family solves extensive-form games and joins that problem, where subclass-restricted methods (backward induction on perfect information) sit beside general ones, mirroring 2-SAT beside CDCL. Fictitious play, regret matching, replicator dynamics, and double oracle compute normal-form equilibria and join nash-equilibrium, relabeled Normal-form equilibrium computation to honestly cover the correlated-equilibrium and evolutionary outputs.

The same techniques were filed on both sides: quorum intersection appears as Quorum replication (there) and Quorum read-write with R+W>N (here); Merkle anti-entropy appears in both. Designing replication and repairing replicas are phases of one contract: keep replicated data consistent and available under failures.

CRDT counters, sets, and registers are a solution family for the replicated-state contract, not a separate problem; a G-counter and an OR-set are not rivals of each other, but coordination-free convergence versus consensus-backed replication is exactly the design rivalry of replication. Per-datatype contracts survive as phrases. Survivor relabeled Replication and replica consistency.

K-fold cross-validation sat in one problem while stratified, nested, and forward-chaining cross-validation sat in another: the same contract, estimate out-of-sample performance to select among models.

AIC, BIC, and MDL are penalized-likelihood rivals of cross-validation for the same decision (which model generalizes best); AIC is asymptotically equivalent to leave-one-out. Survivor relabeled Model selection and generalization estimation.

The membership shows this was the systems question, not the formal atomic-commitment problem: the saga pattern explicitly abandons atomicity. 2PC/3PC vs deterministic execution (Calvin) vs sagas vs RAMP are alternative architectures for one contract, commit transactions across partitions; Calvin exists to eliminate 2PC.

Coverage-guided fuzzing and symbolic/concolic execution generate inputs that expose bugs in the same programs and are benchmarked against each other; concolic testing exists to hybridize them. Hardware ATPG and distributed-system testing remain separate: materially different execution environments and oracles. Survivor relabeled Automated test generation and fuzzing.

Near-exact alias labels: the problem labeled Random graph generation and the problem labeled Random graph models split Watts-Strogatz/Chung-Lu/Kronecker from Erdos-Renyi/Barabasi-Albert/SBM arbitrarily; one contract, sample a graph from a generative model.

Line, circle, and polygon rasterization share one contract, convert a geometric primitive to pixel coverage, with the primitive as the input parameter; the in-repo precedent is Clipping, which already holds polygon and line clipping as phrases of one problem.

Destroy-and-repair is neighborhood search with very large neighborhoods, as the name says; LNS/ALNS belong to the same meta-contract the survivor already owns (discrete optimization by local moves and escapes) beside tabu, annealing, and VNS.

A method-family label (resampling) whose members solve two existing contracts. The permutation test is a standard rival of t and rank tests and joins hypothesis testing. Bootstrap and jackknife estimate uncertainty and bias and join interval estimation, where BCa bootstrap intervals and conformal prediction already live.

The same mathematical contract in two literatures: estimate (ratios of) partition functions. The phrase collision proved it: Free-energy estimation was already a phrase of normalizing-constants via Wang-Landau while free-energy-estimation held FEP/TI/umbrella sampling. Bennett acceptance ratio and bridge sampling are literally the same identity. Survivor relabeled Normalizing constants and free energy.

phraseMoves.reason: Branch and price is a sibling of branch and cut (already filed under integer programming); the split kept the two flagship integer-programming search frameworks from being rivals.

Ant Colony System constructs TSP tours; traveling-salesman already owns the identical contract under the phrase TSP construction (nearest neighbor, greedy edge, savings). Same contract, so the same problem.

Genetic algorithm with edge recombination crossover evolves TSP tours: the same contract traveling-salesman owns. The within-family crossover comparison remains visible on the Genetic algorithm method page.

attachments.reason: Clearing/twist and Ripser compute persistent homology faster: same output contract the problem already covers as Scalable TDA.
The problem already owns the phrase Exact vertex coloring; chromatic number is the same contract.
WAND and block-max WAND prune top-k scoring over inverted lists; Fagin-style threshold algorithms do the same over sorted lists. One contract across the IR and DB literatures.
Query likelihood and divergence-from-randomness are ranking functions on the same benchmark contract as BM25, itself a probabilistic model.
DPR and ColBERT rank documents for queries; dense-vs-sparse is the same rivalry that motivated merging semantic retrieval here.
N-gram models with Kneser-Ney or Good-Turing smoothing and neural language models share the contract: model the probability of text.
Multi-head attention and self-attention entries are sequence-modeling architectures, rivals of recurrent and state-space models on the same contract.
The problem already owns Max-margin classification and Large-scale classification; core vector machines and Pegasos are classifiers at scale.
SVD++ and Slope One predict user-item ratings: the core recommendation contract.
Factorization machines and DeepFM predict user-item response probability: the same affinity-prediction contract phrased for ads.
GRU4Rec and SASRec recommend the next item from interaction history: recommendation with sequential context.
FP-growth and ECLAT mine the frequent itemsets that association rules are built from; the problem already owns Market-basket analysis.
T-learner and X-learner are heterogeneous-treatment-effect estimators: exactly this problem.
The problem already owns the phrase Classifier calibration; Platt scaling and isotonic regression are its standard methods.
The problem exists with the phrase Few-shot classification; MAML and Reptile are its canonical methods.
Curriculum and self-paced learning are training schedules; the problem already owns the phrase Training schedules.
Otsu and adaptive thresholding are the foreground/background case of segmentation, filed in every segmentation chapter.
Quickselect computes order statistics: the problem is literally labeled Selection and order statistics.

added.label: Facility location
added.reason: Split from the clustering-approximation merge: opening costs and a free number of facilities are a materially different objective from fixed-k clustering.

added.label: Polynomial GCD
added.reason: GCD in polynomial rings has its own contract (coefficient growth is the enemy); subresultant PRS vs modular CRT reconstruction is a real rivalry distinct from integer GCD.

added.label: Real root isolation
added.reason: Certified isolating intervals for real roots are a materially different output contract from numerical root approximation; Sturm vs VCA is the standard rivalry.

added.label: Genetic variant detection
added.reason: Calling variants from aligned reads is a standard bioinformatics contract with two real rival methods present.

added.label: Closest pair of points
added.reason: The classic geometry problem; sweep vs divide-and-conquer is the canonical rivalry.

added.label: Polyline simplification
added.reason: Douglas-Peucker vs Visvalingam-Whyatt is the famous rivalry of one contract: fewer vertices, bounded shape error.

added.label: Persistence diagram comparison
added.reason: Bottleneck vs Wasserstein distances compare persistence diagrams: a distance contract distinct from computing the diagrams.

added.label: Persistence vectorization
added.reason: Landscapes vs persistence images turn diagrams into ML-ready vectors: an embedding contract distinct from diagram distances.

added.label: Edge bundling
added.reason: Bundling reroutes the edges of an existing layout to reduce clutter: a post-layout contract with two real rival methods, distinct from node placement.

added.label: Many-light rendering
added.reason: Deferred vs tiled forward shading is the real-time architecture rivalry for scenes with many lights, distinct from shading models and from global illumination.

added.label: All-pairs minimum cuts
added.reason: Gomory-Hu and Gusfield trees answer every s-t cut at once: a different output contract from the single global minimum cut, kept distinct exactly as APSP is from SSSP.

added.label: Transitive closure and reduction
added.reason: Computing the reachability structure of a DAG in either direction (closure, reduction): one contract on the reachability relation.

added.label: Graph comparison and classification
added.reason: Whole-graph kernels and graph edit distance compare or classify entire graphs: a graph-level contract distinct from node-level representation learning.

added.label: Influence maximization
added.reason: Choosing a seed set to maximize spread is a submodular optimization contract, distinct from modeling the spread process itself.

added.label: Contagion and influence spread modeling
added.reason: Independent cascade, linear threshold, SIR, and SIS all model spreading processes over networks: one modeling contract across the marketing and epidemiology literatures.

added.label: Coverage path planning
added.reason: Sweeping every point of a region is a materially different objective from reaching a goal; boustrophedon vs spanning-tree coverage is a real rivalry.

added.label: Shape analysis and skeletonization
added.reason: Distance transforms and medial axes summarize region shape: a morphology contract distinct from segmentation.
